vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: exa
Version: 0.0.2

The skill bundle is benign. All scripts (`code.sh`, `content.sh`, `search.sh`) legitimately use the `EXA_API_KEY` environment variable to authenticate and make `curl` POST requests to the official Exa AI API endpoints (`https://api.exa.ai/search`, `https://api.exa.ai/contents`). The `SKILL.md` provides clear, non-malicious instructions for setup and usage, without any prompt injection attempts. There is no evidence of unauthorized data exfiltration, malicious execution, persistence mechanisms, or obfuscation.

llm.summary: This skill is a straightforward Exa API helper that sends user-provided search queries or URLs to Exa, with no hidden persistence or unrelated local access found.

dimensions.detail: Network access and an Exa API key are proportionate to the stated API-search purpose; no local file harvesting or broad workspace indexing was present.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer, package manager actions, services, or system modifications were found; setup is limited to setting EXA_API_KEY in the environment.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill clearly documents the bash commands and EXA_API_KEY requirement, but users should understand that queries and URLs are transmitted to Exa.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, privilege escalation, background workers, scheduled tasks, or shell behaviors beyond the documented scripts were found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is neural web search, code context, and URL content retrieval through the Exa AI API, and the scripts implement only those API calls.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only if you are comfortable sending search queries, code-search prompts, and requested URLs to Exa using your EXA_API_KEY. Avoid putting secrets, private source snippets, internal URLs, or confidential project details into queries unless your organization permits that use of Exa.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The skill does use local bash scripts, but those scripts are the documented invocation mechanism and contain simple jq payload construction plus curl calls to Exa, not arbitrary command execution.
[SQP-2] expected: The code search script sends the user query to Exa, which is expected for an external search API; the main user consideration is avoiding secrets or proprietary snippets in queries.
[E1] expected: External transmission to api.exa.ai is central to the skill's purpose and is disclosed by the Exa API framing; inspection did not find unrelated exfiltration or hidden destinations.
